title: Selection of routing paths based upon path quality
summary: Multi-hop mesh networks need a principled way to choose among many potential routes to a gateway, but signal strength alone is an unreliable metric. This invention has each routing packet carry an accumulated path quality score updated at every hop, so the receiving node can compare paths and select the one with the best end-to-end quality. It establishes the foundational routing metric algorithm underlying Tropos's mesh platform.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Method for allowing a client to access a wireless system
category: Client Roaming & IP Mobility; Mesh Routing & Path Quality
summary: Connecting a client to a multi-hop wireless mesh requires identifying the access node with the best path to the backbone, even when no direct backbone connection exists. This invention has access nodes detect clients, determine the best routing path through intermediate mesh nodes to the backbone, and facilitate connection — extending coverage beyond direct gateway range through cooperative routing.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Method and system to provide increased data throughput in a multi-hop wireless link
summary: In a multi-hop wireless network, consecutive hops sharing the same radio channel create self-interference that severely limits throughput. This invention provides a distributed channel allocation protocol that assigns different channels to adjacent hops, allowing each hop to operate without interfering with its neighbors, without requiring directional antennas or centralized coordination.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Selection of routing paths based upon routing packet success rate
summary: Packet delivery ratio is a more accurate routing metric than raw signal strength, because a path can appear radio-healthy but still lose a high fraction of packets under real load. This invention has each routing packet carry a cumulative delivery success rate that decreases as it traverses lossy hops, enabling nodes to select the path with the highest end-to-end reliability rather than the strongest individual link.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Minimization of channel filters within wireless access nodes
summary: Dual-radio mesh access nodes capable of operating across N channels would conventionally require N separate bandpass filters — adding cost, size, and weight. This invention shows that a smaller filter bank using wideband or shared filter elements can cover all N channels, reducing hardware complexity while preserving multi-channel capability in mesh access nodes.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi

title: Method and apparatus for monitoring and displaying routing metrics
summary: Network operators managing a large wireless mesh need to visualize path quality across many nodes without being overwhelmed by data points. This invention displays routing metric values for nodes and links but filters the view to show only values within a configurable threshold range, letting operators focus on the links most relevant to current network conditions.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Link layer emulation
summary: Many applications and devices expect a flat Layer 2 broadcast domain, but wireless mesh networks route at Layer 3, breaking protocols that rely on LAN-style broadcasts. This invention uses address translation within the mesh to make the routed infrastructure appear as a simple bridged LAN to connected devices, enabling legacy and broadcast-dependent applications to work without modification.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Providing routing paths for wireless devices
summary: In a multi-hop mesh, nodes need to discover paths to gateways without requiring a centralized directory or manual configuration. This invention uses recursive beacon propagation: each gateway broadcasts its address, and every node that hears it rebroadcasts — forming a distributed connectivity tree that all downstream nodes can use to learn reachable paths without explicit setup.
inventors: Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Access point control of client roaming
summary: When a client moves away from an access point, the AP may continue holding the association even as link quality collapses, blocking the client from connecting to a better AP. This invention has access points actively probe associated clients and issue disassociation frames to any client whose response rate drops below a threshold — proactively freeing clients to roam to the best available AP.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi

title: Wireless mesh network timed commit provisioning
summary: Pushing configuration updates to all nodes of a live mesh simultaneously risks leaving the network in an inconsistent partial-update state if some nodes miss the change. This invention implements an atomic timed-commit protocol: all nodes pre-stage new configuration parameters, then apply them simultaneously at a specified time — and if any node fails to acknowledge the commit command, the entire update is aborted and rolled back.
inventors: Ridwan Peter Sugiarto, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Channel assignments within a mesh network
summary: Adjacent hops sharing the same wireless channel in a mesh network cause self-interference that degrades throughput across multiple hops. This invention assigns alternating channels to consecutive links in a routing path — nodes scan available channels via beacons and select downlink channels that differ from their uplink. Channel selection is distributed and requires no central coordination.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Cyrus Behroozi, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Wireless mesh network verification
summary: After deploying or modifying a wireless mesh, operators need a systematic way to identify underperforming links across the entire network without manually inspecting each one. This invention automatically scans all routing links, identifies those below a quality threshold, and presents a prioritized list to the network manager — enabling efficient targeted troubleshooting of the weakest links first.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Multi-channel mesh network
category: Mesh Routing & Path Quality; Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance
summary: Single-channel mesh networks create interference bottlenecks as all traffic shares one radio frequency. This invention enables nodes to simultaneously use multiple radio channels for routing, so a path to a gateway can combine hops over different frequencies for better throughput and resilience. It allows mesh deployments to leverage 802.11a, b, and g bands in parallel.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Adaptive control of transmission power and data rates of transceivers
summary: Wi-Fi access nodes and their neighbors need to converge on the best combination of transmit power and data rate for each link, but factory defaults rarely match real deployment conditions. This invention has nodes probe N combinations of power and rate, share received-quality results with neighbors, and independently select the combination that maximizes throughput while minimizing interference to adjacent links.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Determining bidirectional path quality within a wireless mesh network
summary: Mesh routing typically evaluates only one direction of link quality, missing the asymmetry common in real-world deployments. This invention has nodes exchange routing packets so both upstream and downstream link quality are measured simultaneously, then uses both metrics to select the optimal path to a gateway. The approach prevents routes that appear strong in one direction but are poor in the other.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, B. William Hong, Roman Arutyunov

title: Determining throughput between hosts
summary: Standard network tools measure latency but not actual achievable throughput between mesh nodes. This invention sends intentionally corrupted ICMP packets alongside normal ones — the ratio of delivered to corrupted packets reveals actual link bandwidth conditions. It enables per-link throughput measurement without dedicated test traffic generators.
inventors: Sam Song Liang

title: Assignment of channels to links of nodes within a mesh network
summary: When a mesh node uses the same radio channel for its uplink and downlink, transmissions on one direction directly interfere with reception on the other, capping effective throughput. This invention assigns different channels to each node's uplink and downlink so adjacent hops in a routing path operate on different frequencies — eliminating this self-interference bottleneck without central coordination.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Probe response determination
summary: When a mobile client scans for access points by broadcasting probe requests, every AP within range typically responds simultaneously, wasting airtime and confusing the client's AP selection. This invention has each AP measure its link quality to the probing client and respond only if the quality exceeds a threshold, so only the AP best positioned to serve the client replies — reducing channel contention and improving initial association.
inventors: Huizhao Wang, Roman M. Arutyunov

title: Remote wireless access node control
summary: Outdoor mesh access nodes deployed in remote locations become inaccessible for management when the primary controller software hangs or fails. This invention adds a secondary controller with an independent remote console interface that can take over management of the node out-of-band, enabling access node recovery without requiring a physical site visit.
inventors: Dev Kumar

title: Client roaming from a first access node to a second access node
summary: During client handoff between access nodes in a mesh network, the new AP lacks the client's session state, requiring the client to re-authenticate and re-negotiate parameters — interrupting active sessions. This invention transfers client information (IP assignment, authentication state, QoS parameters) from the old AP to the new one at handoff time, enabling seamless session continuity as the client moves.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Method of subnet roaming within a network
summary: Mobile devices crossing subnet boundaries in a wireless mesh typically receive new IP addresses, breaking active TCP sessions and VPN connections. This invention keeps a roaming client's IP address, default gateway, and subnet attachment fixed as it moves between access nodes in different subnets, using gateway-mediated routing and tunneling. The mechanism is transparent to client devices and requires no client software changes.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, John Zhuge

title: Mobile access node routing selections through a mesh network
summary: Mobile access nodes on vehicles must continuously reassess upstream routing as link conditions change rapidly with movement. This invention assigns time-decaying weights to routing packets received from upstream candidates and computes a rolling packet success rate, so the mobile node gravitates toward the currently strongest upstream neighbor. The recency weighting ensures stale link measurements do not drive routing decisions.
inventors: Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Mesh network that includes fixed and mobile access nodes
summary: Mixed mesh networks containing both stationary and vehicle-mounted nodes suffer routing instability because mobile nodes are inherently unreliable backhaul. This invention makes nodes consider both link quality and upstream node mobility type (fixed vs. mobile) when selecting routing paths, preferring fixed upstream nodes when quality is comparable. It prevents cascading failures from over-relying on mobile infrastructure for backbone connectivity.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Method and apparatus for monitoring and displaying routing metrics (continuation)
summary: Displaying all link metric values simultaneously across a large mesh network creates visual clutter that makes it difficult to isolate specific performance issues. This invention filters the routing metric display to show only values within a configurable threshold range around a reference point, enabling operators to focus on a specific quality band and identify anomalies against a meaningful baseline.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Regulation of transmission power control to mitigate self-interference
category: Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance; Transmission Power & Rate Control
summary: A mesh node transmitting at high power improves its own link quality but degrades the signal-to-noise ratio of neighboring links, reducing their capacity. This invention tests multiple power and rate combinations while observing the effect on neighboring links, then converges on the lowest power level that maintains acceptable self-performance — balancing individual link quality against the interference imposed on the rest of the network.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Cyrus Behroozi, Jay Kruse, Frederick Dean

title: Wireless routing based on data packet classifications
summary: Mesh nodes equipped with multiple radios on different frequency bands can deliver better quality of service by routing different traffic types over different interfaces. This invention classifies incoming packets by type (such as voice, video, or bulk data) and routes each class through the node interface best suited to its performance requirements — enabling differentiated service across the same physical infrastructure.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Mukesh Gupta, Ramanagopal Vogety, Wenge Ren

title: Multi-channel mesh network (continuation)
category: Mesh Routing & Path Quality; Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance
summary: Choosing the best routing path in a multi-channel mesh requires awareness of channel conditions on all available frequencies, not just the one currently in use. This invention has nodes listen across multiple channels to collect quality indicators from upstream nodes, enabling routing decisions that jointly optimize path quality and channel selection rather than treating them independently.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Mobile node data transmission rate selection
category: Mesh Routing & Path Quality; Client Roaming & IP Mobility
summary: Vehicle-mounted mesh nodes moving between gateway clusters need to anticipate available uplink data rates before committing to a handoff rather than discovering rates only after association. This invention has mobile nodes receive beacons from multiple clusters that advertise gateway transmission rates, enabling pre-handoff rate comparison and selection of the cluster offering the best uplink capacity.
inventors: Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Identification of long links within a wireless network
summary: Wireless mesh links spanning long physical distances consume disproportionate airtime due to propagation delays and the lower data rates needed for long-range operation. This invention estimates link length from signal propagation characteristics without GPS or manual measurement, identifies links exceeding a distance threshold, and flags them for operators — guiding selective upgrades to directional antennas that recover wasted capacity.
inventors: Wenge Ren, Frederick Dean, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Prequalification of potential wireless customers
summary: Wireless service providers need to tell potential customers whether they will receive acceptable coverage before the customer commits to service, but site surveys are expensive. This invention maps the customer's location against a prebuilt network performance database to estimate expected service quality for each application type, enabling accurate self-service prequalification without requiring a physical visit or trial installation.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari

title: Air-time control of wireless networks
summary: In a shared wireless medium, a single node transmitting frequently at high volume monopolizes airtime and starves adjacent nodes of capacity. This invention monitors each node's airtime consumption and enforces a cap when usage exceeds a configured threshold, ensuring fair airtime distribution across all nodes sharing the wireless medium without requiring centralized scheduling.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi, Frederick Dean, Ramanagopal Vogety, Huizhao Wang, Mukesh Gupta, Saar Gillai

title: Determining coverage of a wireless network
summary: Wireless mesh operators need empirical, application-level coverage maps rather than modeled RF predictions to understand where service quality is acceptable. This invention measures performance for multiple application types at many locations around deployed access points, building a location-indexed performance database that accurately shows coverage quality at street level for each service tier.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi, Roman M. Arutyunov

title: Wireless network beacon timing
summary: Access points with multiple SSID personalities each transmit beacons independently, and randomly timed beacons from many co-located APs create significant channel congestion under CSMA/CA. This invention bunches multiple beacon types from the same AP with minimal inter-frame spacing, transmitting them back-to-back within a single interval rather than independently. The technique reduces beacon overhead and wasted airtime in dense mesh deployments.
inventors: Frederick Dean, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Saar Gillai

title: Balancing clusters of a wireless mesh network
summary: Client and node concentration around certain gateways creates overloaded clusters while others remain underutilized, degrading overall network performance. This invention has gateways broadcast their current cluster size in routing packets which nodes relay outward, so new nodes preferentially connect to smaller clusters. The result is passive distributed load balancing across gateways without a central coordinator.
inventors: Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Minimization of channel filters within wireless access nodes (continuation)
summary: Multi-radio access nodes that can operate across many frequency channels conventionally require one bandpass filter per channel — significantly increasing hardware cost and size. This continuation covers a wideband filter bank architecture that achieves multi-channel operation with fewer physical filter elements, enabling economical dual-radio mesh nodes deployable at scale.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi

title: Adaptively setting transmission power levels of nodes within a wireless mesh network
summary: A mesh node cannot directly observe the interference its transmissions cause on neighboring nodes' uplinks, making individual power optimization decisions insufficient. This invention uses the quality of reverse-direction links as a proxy for outbound interference: when upstream link quality at neighbors degrades, the node lowers its transmit power — achieving decentralized cooperative power management without explicit inter-node coordination.
inventors: Mukesh Gupta, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Wenge Ren, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Determination of link qualities between an access point and client devices
category: Network Monitoring & Diagnostics; Client Roaming & IP Mobility
summary: Access points need per-client link quality data to make informed roaming and resource allocation decisions, but polling all clients simultaneously wastes airtime. This invention polls each associated client in round-robin order, maintaining a continuously updated link quality table for all associated clients — providing accurate per-client quality data with minimal overhead.
inventors: Mukesh Gupta, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Wireless mesh network channel selection
summary: Choosing the right operating channel for a gateway cluster requires assessing interference and contention from neighboring Wi-Fi networks and devices. This invention has gateways cycle through available channels to measure contention and noise on each, while access nodes independently measure channel quality via beacon persistence from upstream devices. The dual approach enables both gateway-initiated and node-driven channel selection in a decentralized manner.
inventors: Wenge Ren, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Method of subnet roaming within a network (continuation)
summary: A continuation of the IP mobility architecture covering how access nodes inspect DHCP exchanges to map client MAC addresses to IP assignments in real time. This enables the mesh network to maintain accurate routing for roaming clients without requiring any explicit signaling from client devices, and without disrupting existing IP sessions. It extends the original subnet roaming invention to cover DHCP-based address tracking.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, John Zhuge

title: Adaptively capping data throughput of client devices
summary: Clients with poor wireless links consume disproportionate airtime per bit at low data rates, starving better-connected clients of capacity. This invention monitors each client's airtime-per-bit efficiency and dynamically caps throughput for inefficient clients, protecting network capacity for clients that can use the medium more efficiently — without permanently blacklisting or disconnecting poor-signal clients.
inventors: Cyrus Behroozi, Frederick Dean, Ramanagopal Vogety, Huizhao Wang, Mukesh Gupta, Saar Gillai

title: Conversion of access nodes to gateways within a wireless mesh network
summary: As mesh deployments grow or traffic patterns shift, the original gateway placement may become suboptimal, creating bottlenecks that require human judgment to diagnose. This invention has each access node measure network metrics and report them to a server, which algorithmically identifies nodes that would deliver better aggregate performance if promoted to gateways — automating capacity planning for growing mesh deployments.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari

title: Providing connectivity between subnets of a wireless network
category: Network Management & Provisioning; Mesh Routing & Path Quality
summary: Full-mesh inter-gateway adjacency across many subnets creates routing overhead that grows quadratically with deployment size. This invention has each gateway form adjacencies with a selected subset of gateways in other subnets rather than with all of them, reducing routing state and overhead while preserving inter-subnet reachability across large multi-subnet mesh deployments.
inventors: Ramanagopal Vogety, Mukesh Gupta

title: Monitoring network conditions of a wireless network
summary: Diagnosing performance degradation in a multi-hop mesh is difficult because end-to-end measurements obscure which specific hops are contributing to the problem. This invention uses a test device that systematically measures performance across each subset of hops in the network, isolating the exact hops responsible for degraded end-to-end performance and enabling targeted remediation.
inventors: Kevin Weil, Mukesh Gupta, Amit Saha, Cyrus Behroozi, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Wireless routing based on data packet classification (public safety)
summary: Public safety mesh networks require guaranteed priority access for emergency communications that must be isolated from regular traffic. This invention classifies packets as public safety data and dedicates the licensed 4.9 GHz radio band exclusively to that traffic class on each node — ensuring first-responder communications never contend for airtime with regular network traffic.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari, Mukesh Gupta, Ramanagopal Vogety, Wenge Ren

title: Determining bidirectional path quality within a wireless mesh network (continuation)
summary: Wireless links in mesh networks are frequently asymmetric — strong in one direction but weak in the other — and single-direction routing metrics miss this asymmetry. This continuation of the bidirectional path quality invention covers the specific mechanism for simultaneously measuring upstream and downstream link quality through routing packet exchange, and incorporating both measurements into path selection decisions.
inventors: Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, B. William Hong, Roman Arutyunov

title: Wireless data packet classification of an identified flow
summary: Routing all traffic identically through a mesh ignores the distinct performance needs of different application flows. This invention identifies distinct traffic flows by source and destination address pair, classifies each flow based on observable characteristics, and enables per-flow routing decisions — allowing latency-sensitive flows to be prioritized and bulk flows to be routed over less congested paths.
inventors: Amalavoyal Chari

title: Wireless network beacon timing (continuation)
summary: Access points hosting multiple virtual SSIDs generate independent beacon streams for each, and under CSMA/CA these beacons compete for channel access and create overhead that grows linearly with SSID count. This continuation covers the implementation details of scheduling all beacons from the same physical AP to transmit as a back-to-back burst within a single beacon interval — eliminating per-SSID channel contention overhead.
inventors: Frederick Dean, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna, Saar Gillai

title: Characterizing transmission of access nodes within a wireless network
category: Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance; Network Monitoring & Diagnostics
summary: Coordinating channel assignment across a mesh network requires knowing each node's interference footprint — how many neighbors it can reach (and potentially interfere with) at different transmit power levels. This invention measures how many neighboring nodes receive a given node's signals at various power settings, building an interference characterization that informs network-wide channel and power planning.
inventors: Peter Behroozi, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Characterizing uncoordinated interference of a wireless network
category: Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance; Network Monitoring & Diagnostics
summary: Mesh networks in unlicensed bands share spectrum with neighboring Wi-Fi networks and non-Wi-Fi devices that transmit without coordination, but the source and pattern of this interference is often unclear. This invention has each node collect its own airtime usage history and exchange it with neighbors, using the combined view to characterize whether interference is local or distributed — distinguishing transient noise from persistent external interference sources.
inventors: Kevin Weil, Peter Behroozi, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Mitigation of uncoordinated interference of a wireless access node
summary: Once uncoordinated external interference is detected on a mesh node's current channel, the node needs an automated response to restore link performance without manual intervention. This invention monitors interference levels on each link and evaluates alternative channels and neighbors as candidates for re-routing, then autonomously switches to a lower-interference configuration — enabling self-healing operation when external RF sources appear.
inventors: Kevin Weil, Peter Behroozi, Cyrus Behroozi

title: Roaming of clients between gateways of clusters of a wireless mesh network
summary: When a client roams to a different gateway cluster within the same mesh, the aggregation router must quickly redirect traffic to the new gateway without prolonged black-hole periods. This invention uses time-decaying route cost functions — the old gateway ages its routes while the new gateway advertises fresh ones — so the aggregation router naturally transitions without explicit handoff signaling between gateways. The mechanism scales to large deployments without per-client state at the aggregation layer.
inventors: Mukesh Gupta, Ramanagopal Vogety, Srikanth Chavali, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Identifying correlations within wireless networks
summary: Wireless network performance problems often correlate with external factors — time of day, weather, nearby activity — that are invisible without systematic collection and analysis. This invention correlates observed network performance metrics with concurrent network conditions and activities over time, helping operators identify patterns and root causes of recurring degradation that would otherwise appear as random variation.
inventors: Kevin Weil, Mukesh Gupta, Amit Saha, Cyrus Behroozi, Devabhaktuni Srikrishna

title: Deletion of routes of routing tables of a wireless mesh network
summary: As client devices move and disconnect across a mesh network, routing tables accumulate stale entries that waste memory and can cause traffic to be forwarded toward departed clients. This invention maintains routing tables with logic to delete routes when better alternatives appear or when entries age past a threshold, keeping routing tables accurate as the client population changes dynamically.
inventors: Mukesh Gupta, Ramanagopal Vogety

title: Distributed client information database of a wireless network
category: Network Management & Provisioning; Client Roaming & IP Mobility
summary: Centralized client state databases in wireless networks create single points of failure — when the central server goes down, client connectivity state is lost. This invention selects multiple access points as redundant aggregation nodes that each maintain a synchronized copy of the client database, ensuring client connectivity and seamless roaming survive the failure of any individual aggregation point.
inventors: Ramanagopal Vogety

title: Establishing an IPsec VPN tunnel
summary: Mesh operators serving utility grids and public safety networks need to encrypt sensitive control traffic end-to-end while routing regular traffic natively — without running all traffic through a VPN. This invention configures access nodes to establish IPsec tunnels selectively based on traffic type, enabling encrypted and unencrypted flows to coexist across the same mesh without requiring client devices to manage VPN connections themselves.
inventors: Danu Tjahjono, Rafiq Shaikh, Wenge Ren

title: Updating multicast group information of a client device
summary: Efficient multicast delivery in a mesh network requires each access node to know exactly which clients are subscribed to which groups, but tracking group membership dynamically as clients move and subscribe adds complexity. This invention has each access node monitor client IGMP signaling to track multicast group memberships in real time and propagate membership changes to the mesh, keeping the multicast delivery tree accurate without flooding all nodes with every multicast stream.
inventors: Srinivasa Dommalur Mylarappa, Wenge Ren

title: Mobile access node channel selection within a mesh network
category: Mesh Routing & Path Quality; Channel Assignment & Interference Avoidance
summary: A vehicle-mounted mesh node may enter an RF shadow on its current channel while an adjacent channel remains usable, and waiting for full link failure before scanning for alternatives causes unnecessary disruption. This invention monitors beacon quality on the current channel and proactively scans for better channels when quality drops below a threshold — enabling mobile nodes to switch channels before connectivity is lost rather than after.
inventors: Ramanagopal V. Vogety, Cyrus Behroozi, Amalavoyal Chari

title: Establishing an IPsec VPN tunnel (continuation)
summary: A continuation of the per-traffic-type IPsec VPN architecture for mesh access nodes. This invention covers the tunnel negotiation, authentication, and maintenance sequence handled entirely within the access node — including handling VPN peer authentication and re-establishment after link interruptions — with no requirement for client devices to support VPN protocols.
inventors: Danu Tjahjono, Rafiq Shaikh, Wenge Ren

title: Distribution of multicast traffic through a mesh network
summary: Native IP multicast over multi-hop wireless mesh fails because MAC-layer broadcast uses the lowest basic rate and provides no retransmission, making reliability degrade rapidly with hop count. This invention builds a reliable multicast delivery tree using the mesh's unicast routing infrastructure, enabling high-quality multicast delivery — such as video streaming — to all subscribing clients across a multi-hop deployment.
inventors: Danu Tjahjono, Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, Balaji Rajavelu

title: Encapsulating received multicast traffic in unicast IP packets to support distribution of multicast traffic through a mesh network
summary: IP multicast transmitted natively over wireless mesh networks degrades severely over multiple hops because MAC-layer broadcast uses unreliable delivery. This invention converts multicast to unicast by encapsulating group traffic in packets carrying a special destination address mapped to a multicast group ID, enabling hop-by-hop delivery using the mesh's reliable unicast routing infrastructure. This makes services like video streaming and group push notifications viable across multi-hop mesh deployments.
inventors: Danu Tjahjono, Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, Balaji Rajavelu

title: Wireless mesh access node neighboring channel quality estimation
summary: Assessing whether an adjacent channel would provide better performance than the current one normally requires taking the radio offline to scan — disrupting active traffic. This invention estimates the signal quality on neighboring channels while the radio stays on its current channel by analyzing spectral characteristics, enabling background channel quality assessment and informed channel switch decisions without any service interruption.
inventors: Ali Dabirmoghaddam, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, Wenge Ren

title: Distribution of broadcast traffic through a mesh network
summary: Distributing broadcasts (such as ARP and DHCP) by flooding the entire mesh wastes airtime on nodes that have no clients subscribed to that broadcast type. This invention has access nodes report which broadcast types their associated clients are listening for, enabling the network to forward each broadcast only along a selective delivery tree to subscribed nodes — significantly reducing broadcast overhead in large mesh deployments.
inventors: Danu Tjahjono, Wenge Ren, Amalavoyal Narasimha Chari, Balaji Rajavelu
